extraction_text: King Shalya, incited by his son's words about his unmatched strength and courage, led his chariot forces and charged toward King Yudhishthira.
Yudhishthira intercepted the rapidly advancing army of King Shalya in battle, comparing it to containing a raging flood.
Yudhishthira swiftly shot ten arrows that struck King Shalya's chest. Nakula and Sahadeva each shot three straight-flying arrows.
King Shalya retaliated by shooting three arrows at each of them (Nakula and Sahadeva), sixty sharp arrows at Yudhishthira, and two arrows at each of the angry Madri twins (Nakula and Sahadeva).
Bhima, seeing Yudhishthira under King Shalya's control as if in the jaws of death, rushed to Yudhishthira's aid.
As the brilliant sun moved west, a fierce and terrible battle began.
Bhishma, in a rage, shot superior sharp arrows in all directions at the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas) and their army.
Bhishma's arrows hit Bhima (12), Satyaki (9), Nakula (3), Sahadeva (7), Yudhishthira's arms and chest (12), and he then hit Shikhandin with a roar.
Nakula shot six arrows back at Bhishma, Satyaki shot three, Shikhandin shot seventy, Bhima shot five, and Yudhishthira shot twelve.
Drona shot five sharp arrows like Yama's staff, hitting Satyaki and Bhima.
Satyaki and Bhima each shot three straight-flying arrows back at Drona, likened to hitting an elephant with a goad.

attributes.simile: Hitting an elephant with a goad

extraction_text: Warriors from various regions (Sauviras, Kitavas, Easterners, Westerners, Northerners, Malavas, Abhishahas, Surasenas, Shibis, Vasatis) were slain by arrows but could not kill Bhishma.
Other warriors were slain by the noble-souled Pandavas. Meanwhile, the Pandavas surrounded Bhishma.
Bhishma, though encircled by streams of chariots, remained invincible, likened to a forest fire blazing up and burning enemies.
A metaphorical description: Bhishma's chariot is the fire-altar, his bow the flame, his sword/javelin/mace the fuel, his arrows the sparks—the Bhishma-fire burns the Kshatriya bulls.

attributes.theme: Bhishma as a destructive force of nature

extraction_text: Bhishma covered the enemy army with powerful arrows of various types (gold-feathered, vulture-feathered, ear-arrows, iron arrows).
Bhishma shot down banners and chariot warriors, making the chariot forces look like a Tala forest with tree-tops lopped off.
The great-armed warrior, skilled in weapons, rendered chariots, elephants, and horses driverless in battle.
The sound of Bhishma's bowstring and clapping was like thunder, terrifying all beings.
Bhishma's arrows never missed and never lodged in armor; they were shot from his bow without fail.
